nodes.summary: The discriminant `(d_v f_u + d_u g_v)² - 4 d_u d_v det J` of the dispersion polynomial.
nodes.title: Discriminant of the dispersion polynomial

nodes.summary: Lower end `q₋ = (S - √Δ) / (2 d_u d_v)` of the unstable band of squared wavenumbers, where `S = d_v f_u + d_u g_v` and `Δ = bandDiscriminant` (meaningful when `0 < Δ`, `d_u, d_v > 0`).
nodes.title: Lower end of the unstable wavenumber band

nodes.summary: Upper end `q₊ = (S + √Δ) / (2 d_u d_v)` of the unstable band of squared wavenumbers (meaningful when `0 < Δ`, `d_u, d_v > 0`).
nodes.title: Upper end of the unstable wavenumber band

nodes.summary: At the bifurcation threshold `d_v f_u + d_u g_v = 2 √(d_u d_v det J)` the critical squared wavenumber is `k_c² = √(det J / (d_u d_v))` and `h(k_c²) = 0`.
nodes.title: Critical wavenumber at the Turing bifurcation threshold

nodes.summary: The squared critical wavenumber `k_c² = (d_v f_u + d_u g_v) / (2 d_u d_v)`, the minimizer of the dispersion polynomial (meaningful for `d_u, d_v > 0`; division by zero gives `0`).
nodes.title: Squared critical wavenumber

nodes.summary: `det J = b` for the Gierer–Meinhardt Jacobian (`a + 1 ≠ 0`, `b ≠ 0`).
nodes.title: Determinant of the Gierer–Meinhardt Jacobian

nodes.summary: `det (J - k² D) = h(k²)`.
nodes.title: Determinant of the mode matrix is the dispersion polynomial

nodes.summary: `det J = (a + b)²` for the Schnakenberg Jacobian (`a + b ≠ 0`).
nodes.title: Determinant of the Schnakenberg Jacobian

nodes.summary: The diffusion matrix `D = diag(d_u, d_v)` of a two-species reaction-diffusion system.
nodes.title: Diffusion matrix of a two-species system

nodes.summary: The critical squared wavenumber minimizes the dispersion polynomial over all real `q`.
nodes.title: Critical squared wavenumber minimizes the dispersion polynomial

nodes.summary: The value of the dispersion polynomial at its minimizer: `h(k_c²) = det J - (d_v f_u + d_u g_v)² / (4 d_u d_v)`.
nodes.title: Minimum value of the dispersion polynomial

nodes.summary: For `d_u, d_v > 0`, the dispersion polynomial is negative exactly on the open band `(q₋, q₊)`, which is nonempty iff the discriminant is positive.
nodes.title: Dispersion polynomial is negative exactly on the unstable band

nodes.summary: The dispersion polynomial `h(q) = d_u d_v q² - (d_v f_u + d_u g_v) q + det J`, so that `det (J - k² D) = h(k²)` (`det_modeMatrix`).
nodes.title: Dispersion polynomial

nodes.summary: For `d_u, d_v > 0` and `0 < det J`, the dispersion polynomial is negative at some `q ≥ 0` iff `2 √(d_u d_v det J) < d_v f_u + d_u g_v`.
nodes.title: Turing's criterion for diffusion-driven instability

nodes.summary: A real `2 × 2` matrix has a complex eigenvalue with positive real part iff its trace is positive or its determinant is negative.
nodes.title: Routh–Hurwitz for `2 × 2` matrices

nodes.summary: If the steady state is stable without diffusion (`tr J < 0`, `0 < det J`) and `d_u, d_v > 0`, some Fourier mode is unstable iff `d_v f_u + d_u g_v > 2 √(d_u d_v det J)`.
nodes.title: Turing's criterion

nodes.summary: Under Turing's criterion, every long enough interval `[0, L]` has an unstable Neumann mode.
nodes.title: Large domains pattern

nodes.summary: Every long enough interval has a squared Neumann wavenumber inside a given nonempty open band `(qlo, qhi)` with `0 < qhi`: there is `L₀ > 0` such that for all `L ≥ L₀` some `(n π / L)²` lies in `(qlo, qhi)`.
nodes.title: Long intervals have a squared Neumann wavenumber in any given band

nodes.summary: Only finitely many Neumann modes are unstable on `[0, L]` (for `d_u, d_v, L > 0`, any `J`).
nodes.title: Only finitely many Neumann modes are unstable

nodes.summary: The Fourier mode `e^{μ t} cos(k x) v` is a classical solution of the linearized system `w_t = D w_xx + J w` iff `(J - k² D) v = μ v`.
nodes.title: Dispersion relation

nodes.summary: The complex Fourier mode `w(t, x) = e^{μ t} cos(k x) v` with growth rate `μ`, wavenumber `k` and amplitude vector `v`. (The real part of a complex solution of the real linear system is a real solution.)
nodes.title: Complex Fourier mode

nodes.summary: The Jacobian of the Gierer–Meinhardt kinetics at its steady state, `[[b (1 - a) / (1 + a), -(b / (a + 1))²], [2 (a + 1) / b, -1]]`.
nodes.title: Jacobian of the Gierer–Meinhardt kinetics at its steady state

nodes.summary: `((a + 1) / b, ((a + 1) / b)²)` is a steady state of the Gierer–Meinhardt kinetics when `a + 1 ≠ 0` and `b ≠ 0`.
nodes.title: Gierer–Meinhardt steady state is an equilibrium

nodes.summary: The homogeneous steady state `(u₀, v₀) = ((a + 1) / b, ((a + 1) / b)²)` of the Gierer–Meinhardt kinetics (meaningful for `b ≠ 0`, `a + 1 ≠ 0`).
nodes.title: Steady state of the Gierer–Meinhardt kinetics

nodes.summary: With `d_u = 1`, `d_v = d > 0`, `0 < a + 1`, `0 < b` and `b (1 - a) < 1 + a` (stable without diffusion), some Fourier mode is unstable iff `2 √(d b) < d b (1 - a) / (1 + a) - 1`.
nodes.title: Turing instability of the Gierer–Meinhardt kinetics

nodes.summary: Gierer–Meinhardt activator-inhibitor kinetics in Murray's nondimensional form `(f, g) = (a - b u + u² / v, u² - v)` on `x = (u, v)` (biologically `a, b > 0` and `u, v > 0`; at `v = 0` the division gives the junk `u² / 0 = 0`).
nodes.title: Gierer–Meinhardt activator-inhibitor kinetics

nodes.summary: The Neumann mode `cos(k_n x)` has zero flux at both ends of `[0, L]`: the `x`-derivative of the Fourier mode with wavenumber `k_n = n π / L` vanishes at `x = 0` and `x = L`.
nodes.title: Neumann modes have zero flux at the boundary

nodes.summary: `w` is a classical solution of the linearized reaction-diffusion system `w_t = D w_xx + J w` on `ℝ × ℝ`: `w(t, ·)` is twice differentiable with first and second derivatives `wx`, `wxx`, and `w(·, x)` is differentiable with the prescribed time derivative.
nodes.title: Classical solution of the linearized reaction-diffusion system

nodes.summary: If `tr J < 0` and `d_u, d_v ≥ 0`, mode `k` is unstable iff `h(k²) < 0`.
nodes.title: Mode instability iff the dispersion polynomial is negative

nodes.summary: A Fourier mode grows iff `J - k² D` has an eigenvalue with positive real part.
nodes.title: A Fourier mode grows iff `J - k² D` has an eigenvalue with positive real part

nodes.summary: Mode `k` is unstable iff `0 < tr (J - k² D)` or `det (J - k² D) < 0`.
nodes.title: Instability criterion for a Fourier mode via trace and determinant

nodes.summary: On `[0, L]` with Neumann boundary conditions, if `tr J < 0` and `d_u, d_v > 0`, mode `n` is unstable iff `k_n² = (n π / L)²` lies in the unstable band `(q₋, q₊)` (which requires a positive discriminant).
nodes.title: Finite domain

nodes.summary: Under Turing's criterion the critical wavenumber `k_c = √(k_c²)` is itself unstable (and `0 < k_c²`).
nodes.title: Critical wavenumber is unstable under Turing's criterion

nodes.summary: The Fourier mode of wavenumber `k` is *linearly unstable*: the mode matrix `J - k² D` has a complex eigenvalue `μ` with `0 < Re μ`.
nodes.title: Linearly unstable Fourier mode

nodes.summary: The Jacobian matrix of the Gierer–Meinhardt kinetics at the steady state is `giererMeinhardtJacobian a b`.
nodes.title: Computation of the Gierer–Meinhardt Jacobian at the steady state

nodes.summary: The Jacobian matrix of the Schnakenberg kinetics at the steady state is `schnakenbergJacobian a b`.
nodes.title: Computation of the Schnakenberg Jacobian at the steady state

nodes.summary: In the activator-inhibitor sign pattern (`u` is the activator, `0 < f_u`; then `g_v < 0` follows from `tr J < 0`), diffusion-driven instability of a kinetically stable state forces `d_u < d_v`.
nodes.title: The inhibitor diffuses faster

nodes.summary: The mode matrix `J - k² D` governing the Fourier mode of wavenumber `k` of the linearized system `w_t = D w_xx + J w`, where `J` is the Jacobian of the kinetics at the steady state (convention: `J i j` is the partial derivative of the `i`-th reaction term with respect to the `j`-th species, so `J = [[f_u, f_v], [g_u, g_v]]`).
nodes.title: Mode matrix of a linearized reaction-diffusion system

nodes.summary: If the steady state is stable without diffusion and `d_u, d_v ≥ 0`, diffusion-driven instability forces `f_u g_v < 0`.
nodes.title: `f_u` and `g_v` have opposite signs

nodes.summary: The Neumann wavenumber `k_n = n π / L` of the mode `cos(n π x / L)` on `[0, L]`. Meaningful only for `0 < L`; at `L = 0` the totalized division gives `0`, so every labeled Neumann mode collapses to the homogeneous mode.
nodes.title: Neumann wavenumber on an interval

nodes.summary: `‖w(t, 0)‖` is the amplitude of the mode: `‖w(t, x)‖ ≤ ‖w(t, 0)‖` for every `x`.
nodes.title: Fourier mode is largest at the origin

nodes.summary: The amplitude of a Fourier mode: `‖w(t, 0)‖ = e^{Re μ · t} ‖v‖`.
nodes.title: Amplitude of a Fourier mode

nodes.summary: If the first nonhomogeneous mode already lies beyond the band, `q₊ ≤ (π / L)²`, then no Neumann mode is unstable on `[0, L]`.
nodes.title: Small domains admit no pattern

nodes.summary: The homogeneous mode `k = 0` is stable when the kinetics are stable (`tr J < 0`, `0 < det J`).
nodes.title: Homogeneous mode is stable for stable kinetics

nodes.summary: The Jacobian of the Schnakenberg kinetics at its steady state, `[[(b - a) / (a + b), (a + b)²], [-2 b / (a + b), -(a + b)²]]`.
nodes.title: Jacobian of the Schnakenberg kinetics at its steady state

nodes.summary: `(a + b, b / (a + b)²)` is a steady state of the Schnakenberg kinetics when `a + b ≠ 0`.
nodes.title: Schnakenberg steady state is an equilibrium

nodes.summary: The homogeneous steady state `(u₀, v₀) = (a + b, b / (a + b)²)` of the Schnakenberg kinetics (meaningful for `a + b ≠ 0`; at `a + b = 0` the division gives the junk `v₀ = 0`).
nodes.title: Steady state of the Schnakenberg kinetics

nodes.summary: Turing instability of the Schnakenberg kinetics (Murray 2003, ch. 2). With `d_u = 1`, `d_v = d > 0`, `0 < a + b` and `b - a < (a + b)³` (stable without diffusion), some Fourier mode is unstable iff `2 √d (a + b)² < d (b - a) - (a + b)³`.
nodes.title: Turing instability of the Schnakenberg kinetics

nodes.summary: Schnakenberg's reaction terms `(f, g) = (a - u + u² v, b - u² v)` as a map on `x = (u, v) : Fin 2 → ℝ`, with source rates `a, b` (biologically `a, b > 0`).
nodes.title: Schnakenberg reaction kinetics

nodes.summary: A nonzero Fourier mode grows without bound iff its growth rate has positive real part.
nodes.title: Fourier mode grows unboundedly iff its growth rate is positive

nodes.summary: The Gierer–Meinhardt steady state is stable without diffusion iff `b (1 - a) < 1 + a` (for `0 < a + 1`; then `0 < det J = b` for `0 < b`).
nodes.title: Stability of the Gierer–Meinhardt steady state without diffusion

nodes.summary: `tr (J - k² D) = tr J - k² (d_u + d_v)`.
nodes.title: Trace of the mode matrix

nodes.summary: The Schnakenberg steady state is stable without diffusion iff `b - a < (a + b)³` (for `0 < a + b`; then `0 < det J` automatically).
nodes.title: Stability of the Schnakenberg steady state without diffusion

nodes.summary: If the steady state is stable without diffusion (`tr J < 0`, `0 < det J`), `d_u, d_v ≥ 0`, and `det (J - k² D) < 0`, then the homogeneous mode is stable while mode `k` is unstable.
nodes.title: Diffusion-driven instability (Turing 1952)

nodes.summary: The Turing condition in squared form: `2 √(d_u d_v det J) < S` iff `0 < S` and `4 d_u d_v det J < S²`, where `S = d_v f_u + d_u g_v`. This holds for all real inputs: when `d_u d_v det J < 0`, `Real.sqrt` returns `0` and both sides reduce to `0 < S`.
nodes.title: Turing condition in squared form
Analysis

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
